turnaround_reason: Coty got cut in half (to ~$2.9 from $4.56) on soft Consumer Beauty sales, a heavy debt load (EV ~$6B vs ~$2.6B market cap) and the looming loss of the Gucci fragrance license. It is now recovering as a new ex-P&G CEO deleverages with $750M of Wella-stake proceeds and guides to a return to like-for-like growth in 2H FY26.
bullish_points: Sold remaining 25.8% Wella stake to KKR for $750M upfront, most of which paid down long-term debt — a concrete deleveraging catalyst
New Executive Chairman/interim CEO Markus Strobel (33 years at P&G) brings operating credibility to the reset
Management guides like-for-like sales back to growth in 2H FY26, driven by prestige fragrance launches and growth-market expansion
Prestige fragrance remains a structurally healthy category; the brand portfolio has real cash-generative value
Deep value optically: stock near multi-year lows with analyst targets around $4.86
bearish_points: Debt is still the story — EV more than 2x market cap; equity is a thin slice of a leveraged capital structure
Losing the Gucci license by FY28 is a known revenue and margin headwind with no clean offset yet
Management itself frames FY27 as a 'transition year' — the recovery is slow and back-half weighted
Trailing profit margin is -10%; Consumer Beauty fell 11% in the most recent quarter
catalyst: Return to like-for-like sales growth in 2H FY26 plus continued debt paydown from Wella proceeds lowering the leverage overhang
suggested_trade: Small starter spot near $2.90-3.10; this is a leveraged deleveraging bet, size for the balance-sheet risk
key_risk: Sales growth fails to inflect in 2H FY26 while the Gucci loss approaches, leaving a still-levered balance sheet and forcing further guidance cuts
would_skip_if: You want a clean balance sheet — the leverage makes the equity binary; skip if 2H FY26 fails to show the promised like-for-like inflection
